cards.info: Where is the hypotenuse located in a right triangle?
cards.backInfo: The hypotenuse is the longest side, located directly across from the 90-degree angle.

cards.info: Which leg is the opposite side relative to angle $\theta$?
cards.backInfo: The opposite side is the leg that does not touch the vertex of angle $\theta$.

cards.info: What is the formula for the sine ratio?
cards.backInfo: $\sin \theta = \text{opposite} / \text{hypotenuse}$ (SOH).
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the steps: Identify Angle, Label Sides (Opp, Adj, Hyp), Select Ratio (SOH CAH TOA), and Simplify Fraction.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/6703996a-8670-4144-8d1c-e1b6ef2bc117-1786505989006-307.webp)

cards.info: What is the formula for the cosine ratio?
cards.backInfo: $\cos \theta = \text{adjacent} / \text{hypotenuse}$ (CAH).
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the steps: Identify Angle, Label Sides (Opp, Adj, Hyp), Select Ratio (SOH CAH TOA), and Simplify Fraction.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/6703996a-8670-4144-8d1c-e1b6ef2bc117-1786505989006-307.webp)

cards.info: What is the formula for the tangent ratio?
cards.backInfo: $\tan \theta = \text{opposite} / \text{adjacent}$ (TOA).
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the steps: Identify Angle, Label Sides (Opp, Adj, Hyp), Select Ratio (SOH CAH TOA), and Simplify Fraction.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/6703996a-8670-4144-8d1c-e1b6ef2bc117-1786505989006-307.webp)

cards.info: How is tangent expressed using sine and cosine?
cards.backInfo: $\tan \theta = \sin \theta / \cos \theta$.

cards.info: How do you find a missing side for a trig ratio?
cards.backInfo: Apply the Pythagorean theorem: $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$.

cards.info: What is a common mistake when calculating tangent?
cards.backInfo: Using the hypotenuse in the ratio; tangent only uses the opposite and adjacent legs.

cards.info: Why are sine and cosine values always less than 1?
cards.backInfo: Because the hypotenuse is the longest side and is in the denominator.

cards.info: What happens to side labels if the acute angle changes?
cards.backInfo: The labels for the opposite and adjacent sides swap.

cards.info: Which side of a right triangle is always the longest?
cards.backInfo: The hypotenuse, which is the side opposite the 90-degree angle.

cards.info: In a right triangle, which leg does not touch angle $\theta$?
cards.backInfo: The opposite side is the leg that does not share a vertex with $\theta$.

cards.info: Which leg forms one side of angle $\theta$ along with the hypotenuse?
cards.backInfo: The adjacent side is the leg that forms one side of the angle $\theta$.

cards.info: If $\sin(\theta) = 0.6$, what is the ratio of opposite to hypotenuse?
cards.backInfo: The ratio is $6/10$, which simplifies to $3/5$.

cards.info: In triangle $XYZ$ with right angle $Y$, what is $\cos(X)$?
cards.backInfo: $\cos(X) = XY / XZ$ (Adjacent leg over Hypotenuse).

cards.info: Which trigonometric ratio is calculated as $\text{opposite} / \text{adjacent}$?
cards.backInfo: The tangent ratio ($\tan \theta$).
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the steps: Identify Angle, Label Sides (Opp, Adj, Hyp), Select Ratio (SOH CAH TOA), and Simplify Fraction.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/6703996a-8670-4144-8d1c-e1b6ef2bc117-1786505989006-307.webp)

cards.info: If $\sin(\theta) = 3/5$ and $\cos(\theta) = 4/5$, what is $\tan(\theta)$?
What formula finds the hypotenuse when only the two legs are known?
cards.backInfo: The Pythagorean theorem: $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$.

cards.info: Why is $\tan(\theta) = \text{opposite} / \text{hypotenuse}$ incorrect?
cards.backInfo: Tangent must use the adjacent leg, not the hypotenuse, in the denominator.

cards.info: Can $\cos(\theta)$ ever be $1.5$ in a right triangle?
cards.backInfo: No; cosine must be less than 1 because the hypotenuse is the longest side.
